questions.q: Under which Article was the Right to Education included in the Fundamental Rights, and why?
questions.answer: The Right to Education is added by introducing a new Article 21A in the Chapter on Fundamental Rights in 2002 by the 86th Constitutional Amendment. It was a long standing demand so that all children in the age group of 6-14 years (and their parents) can claim compulsory and free education as a Fundamental Right. It is a major step forward in making the country free of illiteracy.

questions.q: Explain the Right to Freedom of Religion mentioned in the Indian Constitution in six points.
questions.answer: (1) The Constitution of India provides Right to Freedom to all its citizens. It means that Indian State has no religion of its own. Besides the above stated restrictions, the State also has the power to regulate any economic, financial, political or other secular activities related to religion. (2) Freedom of conscience and free profession, practice and propagation of religion: All persons are equally entitled to freedom of conscience and the right to profess, practise and propagate religion freely. (3) Conversion by force or allurement and inhuman practices like human/animal sacrifice and sati are not allowed; the State may restrict this right for public order, morality and health and regulate secular activities linked to religion. (4) Freedom to manage religious affairs: Subject to public order, morality and health, every religious group or any section thereof shall have the right (a) to establish and maintain institutions for religious and charitable purposes; (b) to manage its own affairs in matters of religion; (c) to own and acquire movable and immovable property; and (d) to administer such property in accordance with law. (5) Freedom as to the payment of taxes for promotion of any particular religion: No person shall be compelled to pay any tax, the proceeds of which are specifically used in payment of expenses the incurred on the promotion or maintenance of any particular religion or religious sect. from them the factors which have forced them to reach such a stage. (6) Freedom as to attendance at religious instruction or religious worship in certain educational institutions: (1) No religious instruction shall be provided in any educational institution wholly maintained out of State funds. But no person attending such an institution shall be compelled to take part in any religious instruction that may be imparted there or attend any religious worship that may be conducted there. In case of a minor, the consent of his/her guardian is essential for attending such activities.
